C11.content_en:
Ways to see a competitor's running ads — and how the main tools compare

When you run a client's website or campaigns, you may be asked what ads a competitor runs, and since when. Enter a domain and this tool lists ads pointing to it: format, preview image, advertiser name, first-shown date and last-shown date.

Method / toolPricing modelNotes
This tool (DataForSEO)Pay per request. About $0.002 for 40 results (measured)From a domain: ad format, preview image, advertiser, first and last shown dates. Save as CSV
Google Ads Transparency Center (by hand)FreeGoogle's own tool. Search by site or advertiser name and filter by region and date (per Google's help). You review one ad at a time on screen
Ahrefs Site ExplorerSubscription (see the official site for plans)Includes a paid-search view of a site. Used as part of site analysis
Semrush Advertising ToolkitSubscription (Base and Pro plans; see the official site for prices)A set of tools built for ad research. Broad

Checked in November 2026. Prices change — confirm on each vendor's official site before you buy.

Why use this tool

  • A domain is enough. No need to find the advertiser ID first — type the competitor's site.
  • About $0.002 for 40 results. About 500 lookups per $1, so you can check each client casually.
  • See the run period. First and last shown dates hint at long-running ads versus recent ones (in our nike.com sample, first-shown dates ran from October 2021 to April 2026).
  • A few seconds. We measured about 1.6 seconds for nike.com; quick enough to check before a meeting.
  • Save as CSV. Paste it into a draft report.

When it is not the right fit

  • You want to read every ad's text → the table gives a preview image and a format; the copy is not returned as text.
  • You want only that company's ads → ads pointing to the domain come back from any advertiser, so others mix in (nike.com returned four advertisers, led by Nike, Inc. with 32 of the 40 ads). Use the advertiser column to tell them apart.
  • You want ad results such as clicks or spend → this tool cannot show them.
  • Image and video ads may preview poorly (our sample had 38 text ads, 1 image and 1 video).

This tool does one thing: list the ads pointing to a domain.

FAQ

Why is the advertiser different from the domain owner?

Ads pointing to the domain are collected regardless of advertiser, so overseas entities and agencies can appear.

Can I choose the number of results?

It is fixed at 40 in this version.

What does the country selector do?

It sets the region where the ads were shown. Choose the US for ads shown in the US.

If the last-shown date is today, is the ad live now?

In our nike.com sample, all 40 ads had the fetch date as their last-shown date. That does not guarantee the ad is live.

Can I sign up with a free email address?

No. DataForSEO does not accept free email providers. See What is DataForSEO?

C14.content_en:
Ways to see the top YouTube search results — and how the main options compare

When you are about to start making videos, the first question is what videos lead the search results in the genre you chose. Enter a keyword and this tool lists YouTube's top videos: rank, title, channel, views, upload date and length.

Method / toolPricing modelNotes
This tool (DataForSEO)Pay per request. About $0.002 for 20 results, about $0.01 for 100 (measured)Top videos with rank, channel, views, upload date and length. Save as CSV
YouTube search (by hand)FreeAvailable any time; results change a little each time you look
vidIQFree plan plus paid Boost and MAX (its pricing page lists Boost $19/month and MAX $49/month)Keyword research and video analysis on screen. Broad; a tool for running a channel
YouTube Data APIFree quota (10,000 units a day); a search costs 100 unitsThe official API. You write code to use it. A search is expensive in quota — about 100 a day

Checked in November 2026. Prices change — confirm on each vendor's official site before you buy.

Why use this tool

  • The top results in a table. Views, date and length at a glance show what length dominates.
  • About $0.002 for 20 results. About 500 per $1, so you can test several genre ideas.
  • Seconds, not minutes. Our US sample of 19 results for "side hustle ideas" took 13.7 seconds; earlier tests (in Japan) took about 3–5 seconds for 20 results and about 11 for 100.
  • Pick a country and language. Choose the country and language the results are for (our sample is US English).
  • Save as CSV. Keep a list of videos to study.

When it is not the right fit

  • You want the same order as your own recommendations → this tool returns search results.
  • You want playlists and other non-video blocks → only videos are shown. In an earlier test (measured in Japan with Japanese keywords), one of 20 items was a playlist, so the table can have fewer rows than you asked for, and rank numbers can skip.
  • You want to track a channel's growth → each call gives one snapshot, not a trend.
  • Some videos have no view count (1 of 20 in that earlier Japan test; none of the 19 in our US sample). Missing values stay blank.

This tool does one thing: show what leads YouTube search for a keyword, as many as you ask for.

FAQ

How does the cost change with the count?

In our tests: $0.002 for 20 (also the US sample's cost), $0.006 for 50 and $0.01 for 100.

Why does the table have fewer rows than the count I chose?

Non-video blocks such as playlists are removed.

Is the upload date not shown like "1 year ago"?

The API returns both a text like that and a timestamp. We use the timestamp and show a date.

Is the ranking always the same?

YouTube results change over time, so each fetch can differ a little.

Can I sign up with a free email address?

No. DataForSEO does not accept free email providers. See What is DataForSEO?
